newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai banks,finance firms told to raise provisions.
newsitem.headline: Thai banks,finance firms told to raise provisions.

text.p: Thailand's central bank said on Monday it had ordered commercial banks and finance firms to raise provisions for their sub-standard assets and told 10 finance firms to increase their capital immediately,

Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan also told a news conference that the Thai government, banks and finance firms would go all out to help ease a domestic liquidity crunch faced by the local financial sector. He also appealed for market calm while measures were being taken to help the troubled sector.

Permanent secretary for finance Chatumongkol Sonakul said the 10 finance firms ordered to raise capital currently do not have sufficient provisions for doubtful loans and sub-standard assets and they faced short-term cashflow problems.

Central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond told a press conference that a fund run by the Bank of Thailand is prepared to help these firms raise capital if requested and it will participate in their future management.
"Their capital hikes would help assure creditors of these firms that they can continue to operate soundly," he said.

Rerngchai said the central bank fund would open an 8.25 billion baht credit line for these firms until end-1997 and other companies outside the 10 firms mentioned could also seek assistance from the authorities.
Three of the 10 firms are listed on the Thai bourse - International Trust and Finance Plc, Dynamic Eastern Finance Thailand (1991) Plc, and Sri Dhana Finance and Securities Plc.

Other affected but unlisted companies were Unico Housing Co Ltd, Country Finance and Securities Co Ltd, Royal International Finance and Securities Co Ltd, Thai Fuji Finance and Securities Co Ltd, Thai Finance House Co Ltd, Bangkok Metropolitan Trust Co Ltd, International and Trust Co Ltd.

Governor Rerngchai said the central bank's decision for banks and finance firms to raise provisions for doubtful loans and assets -- to 115 percent and 120 percent respectively from a current 100 percent -- would put the new standard on par with that in the United States.
He said the new requirement would be higher than those in neighbouring countries.
The governor said banks and finance firms would have two years to comply with the higher provision requirement with half of the increase to be made within a year.

Finance Minister Amnuay said Thai financial institutions would need to set aside 50 billion baht ($1.94 billion) as additional provisions in the next two years, of which 24 billion would be made by banks and 26 billion by finance firms and credit companies specialising in housing loans.
"The new provisions requirement is within the capability of these financial institutions to meet," Amnuay said.
